newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks slump on rate hikes, peso and Dow.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks slump on rate hikes, peso and Dow.

text.p: Mexican stocks took a beating for the fourth day in a row Tuesday due to prospects of a big hike in interest rates to prop up the ailing peso and profit-taking on the Dow Jones.
"The market is confused. Political signals are not too positive for international investors, who are also nervous over shifting interest and exchange rates," said an equity analyst.
The leading IPC index closed down 36.21 points, or 1.10 percent, at 3,251.17. Volume continued to be sluggish at 63.2 million shares.
The peso rebounded slightly after a terrible Monday, edging up 1.1 centavo to 7.729 per dollar in key 48-hour trade.
But interest rates were still expected to rise nearly 4 percentage points on the bellwether 28-day Cetes, or Treasury bills, during the central bank's weekly primary auction later on Tuesday.
The prospect of further profit-taking in New York was a bigger worry than the peso for Carlos Ponce, research director at the Santander brokerage.
"The other (adverse) factor was the Dow Jones. Many have been expected it to slide for days now," Ponce said. "With the end of the year coming up, investors don't want to take risks."
Losers dominated the broad market scoreboard, outnumbering winners by 65 to 12 out of 99 stocks traded.

Steel firm Ahmsa and cement firm Apasco bucked the market on expectations of good third quarter earnings. Ahmsa rose 94 centavos (12 cents) to 19.66 pesos ($2.55), while Apasco gained 1.80 pesos (23 cents) to 55 pesos ($7.71).
Technical analysts noted that the IPC broke support at 3,270 points during the session, and located the following support at 3,220 points.
